summary: The sitting governor ran again: Sarah Huckabee Sanders (Republican) won a second term over Fred Love (Democrat) and Colt Shelby (Libertarian).

candidates.name: Sarah Huckabee Sanders
candidates.bio: Sarah Huckabee Sanders is a Republican who has been governor of Arkansas since January 2023, the first woman to hold the office. She was White House press secretary in the first Trump administration from 2017 to 2019. Her first term included the LEARNS Act education law and state tax cuts.

positions.summary: Signed bills in May 2026 lowering the top state personal income tax rate from 3.9% to 3.7% and the top corporate rate from 4.3% to 4.1%.
Announced the Defense Against Criminal Illegals Act, a bill to raise penalties for immigrants in the country illegally who commit additional crimes and to expand the state's sanctuary city ban.
Her 2023 LEARNS Act created education freedom accounts that give families $7,208 this year for private school and homeschool expenses.
Announced a 2023 state lawsuit over the EPA's rejection of Arkansas's air pollution plan, which she called "out-of-control federal overreach."
Said in a January 2024 interview that she is "unapologetically pro-life."

candidates.name: Fred Love
candidates.bio: Fred Love is a Democrat who has served in the Arkansas Senate since 2023 and was its minority whip in 2025. He served in the Arkansas House of Representatives from the 2011 session through the 2021 session.

positions.summary: Says he would invest in infrastructure, workforce training and small businesses and create regional economic hubs.
Says he would protect Medicaid, expand maternal and mental health services and use telehealth in rural areas.
Said in January 2026 that 'due process applies even to illegal immigrants'.
Says he will ensure every student reads on grade level and support teachers with fair pay and resources.

factCheckNote: Winner matches AP-sourced tally (MultiState governors tracker, updated Nov 4, 35 of 36 races called) Summary originally noted that vote shares were from a partial count (about 90%). Shares refreshed on November 25, 2026 from The Green Papers (888,078 votes in total), which does not say the count is certified.
